paragraphs: Initial jump velocities for air, water, and lava/acid, in that order.
The integer and fractional components live in parallel speed/subspeed
tables. !SPF scales the velocity for the selected regional frame rate.
Each movement type selects a 12-byte row: acceleration, maximum speed,
then deceleration. Each value occupies two words; wordSwap places the
integer word before the fractional word consumed by the movement code.
Fuse countdown loaded for newly fired bombs before their explosion sequence.
regional selects the NTSC or PAL reload value.
Accept a newly pressed Start only in gameplay state $08, outside Ceres, with
no power-bomb flag, frozen-time flag or enemy-pause door-transition flag set.
Prime the brightness fade and select state $0C; do not load the pause menu here.
Consume the pending signed 16.16 periodic-damage amount used by heat, liquids,
spikes and several enemy contacts. Varia divides it by two and Gravity by four;
the subtraction borrows from fractional SubUnitEnergy into whole Energy.
Pending periodic damage is one-shot. Clear both fractional and whole words after
application, when time is frozen, or after lethal underflow has clamped health.
Treat energy below 31 as critical. Crossing down queues sound 2 and sets the warning
flag; crossing back up clears it and queues sound 1. Queue rejection can leave the
flag and actual SPC sound out of sync, matching the retained game behavior.
Count consecutive held-jump samples, snapshot held/new input for drawing logic and
compare Energy with its previous sample. A decrease starts hurt flashing when no
flash is active; the conditional debug-invincibility path may restore old energy.
Clear all ten word-indexed projectile/bomb slots, install the inert pre-instruction
and reset global projectile, bomb, cooldown and power-bomb state. Door transitions
and elevators use this to discard the prior room's active projectile runtime.
Zero one slot's complete position, velocity, collision, type, damage, instruction and
drawing state, then install the inert pre-instruction. Slots below $0A decrement the
projectile counter; slots $0A and above decrement the bomb counter, both saturating.
Turn beams and missiles into explosion objects while clearing other projectile types.
A beam first moves its origin to the directional collision edge using its radii;
missiles already use their current origin. Both then receive inert movement.
Visit all ten slots from word offset $12 down to zero. A nonzero instruction pointer
marks an active slot: run its bank-$90 pre-instruction, then its bank-$93 instruction
handler, reloading the shared index after code that may repurpose X.
Tick a positive global projectile cooldown toward zero and canonicalize negative
values to zero. While time is frozen, replace it with 32 every call so firing
cannot become immediately available when the normal tick path is suspended.
Allow a beam only below the five-projectile limit and when the cooldown low byte
is zero. Success reserves ownership immediately by setting cooldown to one and
incrementing the projectile counter; carry reports whether the caller may continue.
Normal missiles share the five-projectile limit with beams. Super missiles require
the count to be below four because firing also creates a linked projectile slot.
Both use the same cooldown test and reserve one counter unit before returning success.
The firing gates inspect only the cooldown's low byte. Higher-byte state is retained
by this historical contract and does not by itself block a reservation.
Redirect permanent Hyper Beam mode to its separate firing path. Otherwise reserve a
beam slot and cooldown through the shared firing gate. A failed charged-enough attempt
stops the resume-charge sound and queues the cannot-fire sound.
Choose the first ordinary slot whose damage word is zero, scanning offsets $00..$08.
The earlier counter gate should guarantee capacity; the retained fallback selects the
last ordinary slot if counter ownership and damage occupancy disagree.
Resolve pose-dependent origin/direction, set the projectile-invincibility window and
trail timer, then combine equipped beam bits with the live-projectile flag. Beam type
selects its sound and bank-$93 damage/instruction record.
Charge Beam or a newly pressed shot uses the ordinary per-beam cooldown table. Without
Charge Beam, a held auto-fire continuation uses the separate auto-fire table. Both
tables are byte-indexed by the low six projectile-type bits.
Begin with zero velocity for an immediate spawn-point block collision. Non-wave beams
may become an explosion and return before motion is installed. Surviving beams select
a pre-instruction by beam combination and then receive directional velocity.
The twelve valid low-nibble beam combinations choose straight/no-wave motion, the
uncharged ice-wave handler, or the shared wave/plasma/spazer handler.
Reserve a normal projectile slot through the shared beam gate. A failed attempt with
at least 16 ticks of prior charge stops the resume-charge sound and queues cannot-fire
feedback; shorter failed attempts return silently.
Choose a zero-damage ordinary slot, resolve origin/direction, then retain only the
charge-equipment bit and low beam combination before adding the live and charged-shot
type flags. The combination selects charged sound and bank-$93 projectile data.
Charged shots deliberately use `ProjectileCooldowns_Uncharged`, indexed by the low
six type bits after construction. The table name is retained source vocabulary; this
routine's type still has the charged bit set.
Probe the spawn point before installing motion. Non-wave beams that immediately become
an explosion skip movement setup; surviving beams select a pre-instruction and receive
directional velocity. Every completed construction path starts a four-tick glow.
All charged wave combinations use the shared wave/plasma/spazer/charged-ice-wave
handler. Charged combinations without wave use the straight no-wave handler.
Fire on either the current new-shot edge or the drawing-time copy of the preceding
edge. The shared gate reserves cooldown/counter ownership before ammunition and actual
slot occupancy are checked.
Undo the shared firing gate's counter reservation when selected ammunition is zero or
the five damage words contain no free slot. A later pose-direction failure follows the
retained direct-return path instead; normal gameplay poses supply a direction.
Choose the first zero-damage ordinary slot, resolve pose-dependent origin/direction,
set the 20-tick interaction window, and consume one missile or super missile only after
origin creation succeeds.
Move HUD selection 1/2 into the projectile category byte, add the live flag, and choose
the corresponding non-beam sound unless a cinematic suppresses it. Then initialise
velocity, bank-$93 projectile data, and missile/super-missile motion behavior.
Select missile or super-missile pre-instruction from category bit $0200. The category
nibble then indexes the byte cooldown table. Auto-cancel clears selection immediately;
otherwise the last unit of the selected ammunition clears it.
Find a second zero-damage ordinary slot, mark it as a live super-missile link, and copy
the primary projectile's position and direction before loading link data and behavior.
The earlier super-missile firing limit is what normally guarantees this slot.
Pack the link slot offset into the primary projectile variable's low byte while retaining
its high byte, then increment the ordinary projectile counter for the second owned slot.
While the configured shot button is held, route HUD item 3 to power bombs and every
other selection to the normal-bomb path. Releasing shot cancels any nonzero charge/flare
state, restores the suit palette and queues the cancellation sound.
Ask the bomb/spread gate to reserve ownership. On success, scan the five bomb slots at
offsets $0A..$12 for a zero type word; the counter gate should make the retained final-slot
fallback unnecessary during consistent runtime state.
Create category-$05 bomb state at Samus's position with direction zero and the regional
fuse reload. Bank $93 supplies damage/script data; the bank-$90 pre-instruction handles
the fuse, and category 5 selects its byte cooldown.
Reject while the signed active-power-bomb flag is negative. Otherwise reserve a bomb
slot on a new shot press, require ammunition, decrement it, and mark power-bomb activity
with $FFFF before constructing the slot.
Find a zero-type bomb slot and move HUD selection 3 into the type's category byte. Use
Samus's position, direction zero and the regional fuse, then install power-bomb data,
pre-instruction and category cooldown.
After construction, an auto-cancel request clears both selection and request. Otherwise
power bombs remain selected while ammunition remains and clear after the final unit.
Bombs require Morph Ball Bombs equipment bit $1000. Before 60 charge ticks, or while
any bomb slot is already counted active, tail into ordinary bomb reservation. A fully
charged state with zero active bombs instead manages bomb-spread release.
While controller bit $0400 remains held, increment the spread timeout until its top two
bits both become set. Releasing that bit or reaching the timeout fires the spread,
restores the suit palette and queues the charge-release sound. No single slot is reserved.
Ordinary and power bombs require a real new shot edge. The first active bomb bypasses
the later-bomb limit/cooldown checks; subsequent reservations require fewer than five
active bombs and a zero cooldown low byte.
Success increments both cooldown and bomb count before returning carry set. The caller
replaces that provisional cooldown after construction. Failure cancels nonzero charge
state, clears flare animation, restores the suit palette and returns carry clear.
Tick the current bomb slot's fuse. At 15 ticks remaining, advance its instruction cursor
by $1C bytes to the late-fuse animation segment. At zero, queue the bomb sound and replace
the slot with its bank-$93 bomb-explosion instruction list.
Tick the power-bomb fuse and use the same $1C-byte late-fuse animation advance at 15.
When the fuse reaches zero, publish the explosion origin, enable HDMA objects and spawn
the global power-bomb explosion effect.
Preserve X, Y, status and data bank around the long HDMA/effect calls, then write $FFFF
to the slot timer. The retained routine continues through its normal return this frame.
A zero slot timer waits while the separate global power-bomb flag remains nonzero. Once
the effect clears that flag, release the projectile slot through the shared clear routine.
Use the current pose's eight-byte definition record unless a one-shot transition shot
direction is pending; that override is consumed immediately. Direction bytes with a zero
high nibble are normal shot directions.
Store direction in the selected slot, use its low nibble to index signed X/Y origin
offsets, and subtract the pose definition's Y offset. Most poses use the default tables;
running and the two moonwalk poses use their shared alternate tables.
Direction marker $10 asks the previous different pose for a usable direction. Any other
nonzero high-nibble marker, or another special marker from that fallback pose, rejects
firing, decrements the earlier projectile-counter reservation and returns carry set.
Use the ordinary beam firing gate, scan the five normal slots for zero damage, and
resolve pose-dependent origin/direction. A rejected origin already undoes the gate's
counter reservation through the shared position routine.
Assign fixed type $9018, queue the charged sound selected by its plasma low nibble, and
load the matching charged bank-$93 record. Probe initial wave collision before forcing
damage to 1000 and installing Hyper Beam behavior and velocity.
A successful shot sets cooldown 21, a charged-glow word of $8014, and flare animation
frames/timers for the Hyper Beam presentation. Flare counter $8000 selects its separate
animation path.
Ignore zero/negative ordinary charge state, but route permanent Hyper Beam mode to its
separate countdown animation. On the first ordinary charge tick, initialize the main
flare and two spark components.
After 15 charge ticks, animate component 0; at tick 16 queue the charging sound. Delay
tables use byte $FF to restart at frame zero and $FE followed by a byte to move the frame
cursor backward. At 30 ticks, also animate components 2 and 4.
Hyper Beam walks components 4, 2 and 0 downward. Expired timers decrement frame counters;
nonzero frames reload three ticks. Component 4 reaching frame zero clears the global flare
counter while all components are still offered to the shared drawing helper.
Combine the component's frame byte with a facing-specific index base to select a bank-$93
flare spritemap. The current pose supplies vertical offset and shot direction; marker $FF
or $10 suppresses drawing.
Direction selects signed flare origin offsets. Running uses alternate tables; other
movement uses defaults. Convert world position to layer-1 screen coordinates and subtract
the pose Y offset before submitting a visible byte-page Y coordinate.
In the rotating Ceres room, temporarily transform Samus's position through the shared
rotation helper, calculate/draw the flare from that transformed position, then restore
the original world coordinates.
Clear all three flare/spark frame words and all three timers. Charge counter and suit
palette are managed by the caller because cancellation, firing and Hyper Beam use
different presentation transitions.
Resolve the missile type's low-nibble data index, but deliberately seed base speed with
zero. Preserve the selected projectile slot in both scratch conventions before entering
the shared direction dispatcher. Missile acceleration supplies the launch speed later.
Clear both subpositions, reduce the direction to its low nibble, and dispatch through ten
word pointers. Directions 0/9 share up and 4/5 share down; the eight directional helpers
combine base speed with selected pieces of Samus's recent movement.
The variable high byte is both the initialized marker and eventual base-speed word. Until
it becomes nonzero, add MissileInitializedBitset once per update and return. On the crossing
tick, initialize directional velocity; a super missile also creates its linked projectile.
Multiply direction by four to select an X/Y acceleration pair. Type bit $0200 chooses the
super-missile table; otherwise use ordinary missile acceleration. Add both signed words to
the live velocities while preserving the caller's X and Y registers.
Upward shots negate base speed and optionally add a correction derived from the unaligned
word at ProjSpeed_SubDistanceSamusMovedRight+1. Its bytes span two movement fields; the
routine's shift/sign operations and retained low-byte contamination are documented as-is.
Right/down components add base speed to unaligned recent-movement words. These loads do not
represent clean 16-bit speeds: each starts at the second byte of one RAM field and consumes
the first byte of its neighbor. Preserve that original byte ordering when reviewing behavior.
Leftward shots negate base speed, then add CameraYSubSpeed+1. That unaligned word combines
the high byte of camera Y subspeed with the low byte of distance-moved-left; the apparently
unrelated low byte is real source behavior, not a normalized movement value.
Diagonal helpers calculate each axis independently using the same horizontal/vertical paths
as cardinal shots. Up-left combines the shifted upward correction with negated base speed
and the CameraYSubSpeed+1 leftward overlap; other diagonals use their corresponding pair.
Run link handling only for live super missiles ($0200) or their explosion category ($0800),
and only after the variable high byte marks initialization complete. The variable low byte
is the linked projectile slot offset used for the auxiliary collision probe.
At vertical speed magnitude $0B00 or greater, derive an offset from the integer speed minus
ten, place the link behind the primary's current position, and move the link through the
ordinary missile collision helper. Slower live supers simply copy primary Y into the link.
The horizontal path has the same category, initialization and linked-slot gates. It uses
absolute X velocity to decide whether an auxiliary probe is needed, then temporarily makes
the linked slot current while calling the horizontal missile mover.
Explosion category $0800 clears the linked projectile on both fast and slow paths instead
of synchronizing its coordinate. Live category $0200 keeps the link: fast paths retain the
collision-helper result, while slow paths copy the primary coordinate directly.
A nonzero direction high nibble is the shared deletion flag. Otherwise spawn a trail every
four updates, add the direction's X/Y acceleration pair, run the matching non-wave collision
wrapper, and finally cull the beam against the expanded viewport.
Cardinal wrappers move on one axis. A diagonal non-wave beam moves horizontally first and
skips its vertical move when horizontal collision returns carry set, preventing a second
block interaction after the beam has already collided.
Ordinary missiles share the deletion flag, four-update trail cadence and direction-indexed
projectile acceleration used by beams. They then call the separate launch/acceleration state
machine, dispatch missile collision by direction, and finish with viewport culling.
Direction is doubled for the projectile-acceleration word tables, then halved back to its
numeric value across AccelerateMissile, and doubled again for collision-pointer dispatch.
The shared ProjectileIndex reloads the live slot after trail code may repurpose X.
Missile cardinal wrappers move one axis. Diagonals call horizontal movement first and call
vertical movement only when no horizontal collision occurred, mirroring the non-wave beam
ordering with missile-specific collision helpers.
A live super missile emits trails every two updates, accelerates through the shared missile
state machine, and dispatches a collision wrapper by direction. A deletion flag or successful
offscreen cull enters group cleanup instead of leaving its linked slot behind.
Scan all five ordinary projectile offsets from $08 through $00 and clear every category
$0200 entry. This removes both the primary and linked representation; it also means cleanup
is category-wide rather than limited to one stored link back-reference.
Move the primary horizontally, then immediately update horizontal link collision. If clear,
move vertically and update the vertical link path; if horizontal movement collided, still run
horizontal link cleanup/synchronization but skip the vertical axis.
The link normally has no independent movement. If its direction high nibble requests deletion,
clear the link, then perform the same five-slot category-$0200 sweep as primary cleanup so a
link-side collision cannot leave the primary active alone.
Normal and power bombs first honor the common direction-high-nibble deletion flag. Live
slots tick their respective fuse/effect handler, then run the shared bomb/explosion block
collision routine every update; fuse handling does not replace collision handling.
Wave/plasma/spazer and charged ice-wave beams spawn trails every four updates before joining
the common wave mover. Uncharged ice-wave uses a three-update trail cadence and deliberately
falls through to that same mover after reloading the slot.
Add the same direction-indexed X/Y acceleration pairs as non-wave beams, but dispatch to
wave-specific movement helpers that can pass through compatible blocks. Diagonal movement
still processes horizontal collision first and suppresses vertical movement on carry set.
Hyper Beam honors the same deletion flag, then jumps directly to common wave movement.
It does not pass through either periodic trail-entry routine; its separate firing/flare
presentation owns the visible effect state.
Compare world position against layer-1 scroll using signed screen-relative bounds. X and Y
must each lie in [-64, 320); otherwise clear the slot and return carry set. A surviving
projectile returns carry clear so super-missile code can distinguish group cleanup.
The low beam-type nibble selects four-byte speed records. Direction selects cardinal versus
diagonal speed, then the shared directional initializer combines that base with the retained
recent-movement words. The long-call wrapper establishes bank $90 and restores it on return.
Left/right pointer tables are indexed by a doubled normalized type. Beam combinations occupy
$00..$1F, missile and super missile use $20/$21, and SBA trail variants use $24..$26.
Each entry independently selects one instruction list for each half of the trail pair.
Normalize beams to their low six type bits. For non-beams, only category nibbles below three
are eligible; adding $1F maps missile/super categories 1/2 to table entries $20/$21. Other
categories return carry set without allocating a trail.
Scan eighteen paired trail slots from word offset $22 down to zero. A zero left timer owns
pair liveness. Initialize both timers to one, install left/right scripts, copy the projectile
origin through SetProjectileTrailPosition and return carry clear; exhaustion returns set.
Each active half pre-decrements its timer. At zero, negative list words are bank-$90 command
addresses invoked with a synthetic return to the fetch loop; nonnegative words are durations
followed by tile/attribute data. A zero duration ends that half of the trail pair.
Draw each active half only while the low-OAM cursor is below $200 and both screen-relative
coordinates have high byte zero. A visible half appends one four-byte low-OAM entry; the
right half repeats the same interpreter and visibility checks independently.
Frozen time still draws both active halves with the same OAM capacity and byte-page visibility
checks, but never decrements timers, interprets commands or advances script cursors. Trail
animation and scripted position changes therefore pause while presentation remains visible.
The trail interpreter's position commands use Y as the paired-slot offset. They increment
either half's Y for downward drift or decrement the left half for upward drift, then RTS
to the synthetic interpreter return without consuming a parameter word.
Snapshot the current charge counter before any update so firing failure paths can decide
whether to stop the charging sound. Hyper Beam or a loadout without Charge Beam simply
fires an uncharged/Hyper shot while the bound shot button is held. With Charge equipped,
held input advances toward 120; tick one fires the initial uncharged shot, and 120 attempts SBA.
A pending pose-transition direction forces immediate release logic rather than advancing
charge. Counters below 60 fire uncharged; 60 or more fire charged. Both paths clear the
charge counter and all three flare components before tail-jumping to construction.
Releasing with a nonzero counter chooses uncharged below 60 and charged at or above 60.
These are tail jumps: the selected firing routine restores the PHP frame. A zero counter
returns without creating a shot.
Carry clear leaves charge/flare state intact, allowing another attempt while held. Success
clears charge and component state and reloads the normal suit palette because the SBA now
owns projectile presentation.
An SBA is available only while power bombs are the selected HUD item. The low equipped-beam
nibble selects twelve dispatch entries; only pure wave, ice, spazer and plasma combinations
have constructors. Mixed/normal power combinations return carry clear.
Subtract the combination's table cost before dispatch and clamp underflow to zero. Pure SBA
entries cost one; disabled combinations cost zero. The dispatcher itself does not reject an
underflowing count, relying on HUD selection to represent usable power-bomb inventory.
After the selected constructor returns, zero remaining power bombs clear both HUD selection
and its auto-cancel request. Carry is intentionally left exactly as the constructor supplied
so charge control can distinguish success from retryable failure.
Create four live charged projectiles in slots 3..0 at the corners of a 256-pixel square
centered on Samus. Each starts with wave-SBA behavior, zero direction/X speed/phase scratch
and a regional Y timer before bank-$93 SBA initialization.
Publish four owned projectiles, reuse the normal beam-combination cooldown, set shared angle
delta +4 and queue library-1 sound $28. The signed X/Y offset tables enumerate the four
square corners in slot order and are data within this guarded constructor scope.
Reject a second ice SBA while slot zero is in either its main orbit or ending expansion.
Otherwise create four initialized charged projectiles with origin angles $00/$40/$80/$C0
and the regional main-phase timer.
Set shared angular step to +4 while facing right or -4 while facing left, queue sound $23 and
return carry set. Counter/cooldown publication mirrors the other four-projectile SBAs.
Create four slots with direction 5, radius/speed word $28 and alternating angular deltas.
Slots 0/1 use the equipped charged-beam type and SBA initializer; slots 2/3 are special
type $8024 trail projectiles initialized through the shinespark-echo path.
Only the two special trail slots start with trail timer four; the two main projectile slots
start at zero. Per-slot deltas alternate +4/-4. Global SBA angle delta is cleared, sound $25
is queued and carry reports success.
Reject a second plasma SBA while slot zero already runs its pre-instruction. Otherwise seed
four charged projectiles at the cardinal angle bytes, with radius/speed $28 and zero secondary
velocity, then use bank-$93 SBA initialization.
Like ice, facing chooses shared angular step +4 or -4. Publish four owned slots and the normal
beam cooldown, queue sound $27, and return carry set; duplicate rejection returns clear before
any slot or inventory construction work.
A lifecycle deletion flag queues sound $24 and clears the slot. Otherwise emit trails every
four updates and use the slot's byte angle with fixed radius $20 to position it around Samus
through Math_90CC39.
Store world position at Samus plus the calculated X/Y components, then advance the angle by
the facing-derived signed shared delta and mask it to one byte. The four slots therefore
remain quarter-turn separated while orbit direction follows firing-facing.
Tick the regional phase countdown stored in Y velocity. At zero, switch this slot to ending
behavior, seed expansion radius $28 and queue sound $24. Every main-phase update holds beam
cooldown at two and clears charge so ordinary firing cannot overlap the SBA.
Ending behavior keeps the four-update trails and calculates orbit position from the current
byte radius in X velocity. After drawing position, advance angle by the shared signed delta
and expand radius by eight, masking both state words to a byte.
Clear a slot once screen-relative X leaves [-32, 288) or Y leaves [16, 256). These asymmetric
bounds are tested after storing each world coordinate; an out-of-range axis exits before angle
or radius advances for that update.
A surviving ending slot refreshes cooldown two and clears charge just like the main orbit.
Crossing either viewport bound uses the shared clear routine, eventually releasing all four
owned slots and allowing a later ice SBA.
Delete on a direction-high-nibble flag or when the regional countdown in Y velocity reaches
zero/nonpositive state. Deletion queues sound $29 and clears that slot. A live slot preserves
its previous X velocity and the current Y-velocity word before motion.
Steer horizontally toward Samus by adding or subtracting $40 from packed 8.8 velocity while
inside the retained $F801/$0800 limits. Convert that packed word into signed integer and
fractional components, then add them to the projectile's 16.16 X position.
The projectile variable is the packed vertical velocity. Steer it toward Samus under the same
$F801/$0800 limits, split it into 16.16 movement components and update Y subposition/position.
The earlier copy to $24 is retained source behavior but is not consumed later in this routine.
Only slot offset six owns the crossing sound. Compare current X-velocity sign with the saved
pre-steering sign and queue sound $28 when it changes in either direction. Other slots skip
this presentation event even though they use identical homing motion.
Every surviving update refreshes beam cooldown to two and clears ordinary charge state. This
keeps firing/flare presentation suppressed until all wave-SBA slots expire or are deleted.
Clear a slot when its direction high nibble is marked; otherwise keep firing locked and use
the byte angle in projectile variable with the byte radius in X velocity to position the
projectile around Samus through Math_90CC39.
Advance the angle by the facing-derived shared delta, preserve Y as the projectile index and
dispatch through Y velocity as a word-table phase number: 0 expands, 1 contracts and 2
disperses. The phase routines deliberately receive the slot in Y after X becomes an offset.
Expand the byte radius by four each update. Once it reaches $C0, set the phase word in Y
velocity to one so the next update contracts; the radius remains $C0 for that transition.
Contract the byte radius by four each update. The first radius below $2D selects phase two,
so ordinary four-unit progression changes phase at $2C and dispersal begins next update.
While screen-relative X remains in [-32, 288) and Y in [16, 256), increase the byte radius
by four so the orbit disperses outward. Crossing any bound clears the current slot through
the shared projectile cleanup routine.
A live slot emits a trail every four updates, calculates its horizontal circle component from
the angle/radius fields and delegates vertical position plus phase transitions to a handler.
The phase value is already a byte offset: 0 circles, 2 flies inward and 4 flies outward.
Handlers receive the projectile slot in Y because X becomes the phase-table offset. Every
surviving main update refreshes cooldown two and clears charge after the phase returns.
A deletion flag dispatches by projectile-slot offset and clears a linked pair: 0 with 4 or 2
with 6. Each helper restores the triggering X after clearing its partner, preserving the
caller's slot convention even though this update returns immediately.
Finish the circular position by adding the calculated Y component to Samus, then advance the
byte angle by this slot's signed delta. At exact angle $80, expand radius to $A0, reduce the
alternating angular steps to +/-2, clear direction and select phase offset two.
Orbit around a point 114 pixels above Samus while reducing radius by five. Crossing screen Y
16 converts immediately to the ending projectile. At radius zero, reverse each slot's angular
direction, rotate its angle by $80 and select phase offset four; slot zero queues sound $26.
Continue around the elevated point with the reversed angular delta while increasing radius by
five. Convert to the ending projectile at screen Y below 16 or once radius reaches $60.
Shift slots 0/1 right 16 pixels and slots 2/3 left 16, set direction five, restart the trail
timer and install the ending pre-instruction. Main slots 0/1 are converted to special type
$8024 and reinitialized; slots 2/3 already have that type from construction.
The ending projectile keeps a four-update trail cadence and falls eight pixels per update.
Clear it once screen-relative Y reaches $F8; a surviving slot continues to lock ordinary beam
fire and erase charge state until the falling group has left the viewport.
Facing-forward poses 0 and $9B skip cooldown, item switching and movement-specific HUD work
and run projectile handling directly. Other poses tick cooldown, process selection changes
and dispatch by the low movement-type byte before deciding whether frozen time blocks projectiles.
The 28 movement types select standard, morph-ball, grapple, turn, transition, grabbed or
restricted behavior. A movement handler may update weapon state even when frozen time then
prevents the shared projectile update.
An active grapple overrides the selected HUD item. Otherwise frozen time forces the X-ray
path; normal time doubles selected item 0..5 into the handler table. This keeps an already
active grapple and X-ray's freeze state authoritative over ordinary weapon selection.
Nothing and power bombs share charge/beam handling; missiles and supers share their firing
path. Grapple and X-ray have dedicated handlers. The seventh turning entry is retained but
cannot be indexed by the valid selected-item range.
Delegate grapple ownership to its long-call handler. The wrapper intentionally contributes no
selection, projectile or charge logic of its own.
A transition-supplied shot direction permits standard weapon handling during a turn. Without
one, cancel an active grapple by selecting its hit-nothing state and suppress ordinary firing.
Transition poses $DB..$F0 suppress HUD weapon work and poses $F1+ use standard handling. The
crouch/stand/morph/unmorph group indexes a byte table: zero uses standard handling, while one
joins the restricted handler that first resolves grapple state.
Spin/wall jump, knockback, damage boost, shinespark and crystal-flash-family states do nothing
when grapple is inactive. If grapple is active, cancel it and run standard handling for that
update; subsequent restricted updates return immediately.
Held dash runs the X-ray handler. Releasing dash falls back to the nothing/power-bomb handler,
which restores the ordinary charge/beam path without changing the selected HUD item here.
Draygon's morph-ball-held pose $DF uses morph-ball weapon handling. Other grabbed poses retain
the standard selected-item handler.
A new cancel press selects nothing and clears auto-cancel. A new select press advances through
the six candidates with wraparound. Held cancel is recorded separately so a newly accepted
selection can become the auto-cancel item.
Each candidate handler reports availability through carry: clear accepts it, set advances to
the next item and wraps after X-ray. The nothing handler always succeeds, so the scan has a
defined terminus even when every inventory-backed item is unavailable.
A changed selection resets arm-cannon toggle state to one. An unchanged selection advances
that state but clamps it at two. The arm-cannon state machine uses this settling signal to
reconcile open/closed presentation with the accepted item.
Candidate order is nothing, missiles, supers, power bombs, grapple and X-ray. The handlers
validate ammo/equipment and clear charge presentation when accepting a new selection.
Nothing is always selectable. Clear charge and flare animation, restore the suit palette and
return carry clear so availability scanning stops.
Reject missiles with carry set when live ammo is zero. An available selection clears ordinary
charge presentation and returns carry clear.
Reject supers with carry set when live ammo is zero; otherwise clear charge presentation and
accept the candidate.
Reject power bombs when live ammo is zero. Acceptance follows the same charge/flare/palette
cleanup used by missiles and supers.
Equipment bit $4000 gates grapple availability. If grapple is inactive, accepting it restores

left initial collision probing. The helpers restore the slot from ProjectileIndex because X

the wave-aware block movement path so pass-through behavior is applied during the spawn probe.

the same axis priority as ordinary beams while changing the collision semantics.

initial probe from the otherwise zeroed firing velocity.

beam pre-instruction from its low beam nibble. Reflected types remain non-damaging by default.

reinitializing the primary, restore super-missile runtime and seed `$00F0`; later missile
initialization can construct a fresh link for the reflected trajectory.

the flare counter and all flare animation components; lower nonzero charge clears silently.

movement and the shared collision/low-energy ending check. Energy drains by one only while the
pre-drain value is at least thirty.
Diagonal flight runs horizontal movement before vertical movement, then the shared ending check
and the same thresholded one-energy drain. Both axes can therefore publish collision state in
one update before termination is evaluated.

shares collision/low-energy termination and the one-energy drain used by the other directions.

from the ordinary left/right Samus speed calculators.

nonzero result and skip block movement. Otherwise right flight moves directly; left flight
negates the magnitude back to a signed displacement before using the shared right-move helper.

displacement before collision processing.

cap its integer word at fifteen for solid-enemy collision. On success, negate it back to upward

mirrored for downward deltas here.

seven, clear shared motion/position state and invincibility/knockback, and preserve the demo pose
input handler while replacing ordinary input with a no-op. Success returns carry clear.

ten updates move her upward twenty pixels before frame six is installed and the raised Y position
is saved for later descent.

coordinates on Samus and enable/spawn the crystal-flash HDMA objects under explicit register saves.

invincibility and knockback timers after the selected consumer returns.

ticks, reload the ten-count timer and advance to super missiles.
Consume one super missile and restore fifty energy every eight serviced frames. Ten ticks reload
the phase timer and advance to power bombs.
Consume one power bomb and restore fifty energy on the same eight-frame cadence. The tenth tick
installs finish movement/default drawing and selects animation frame twelve instead of advancing
to another ammo phase. Across all three resources the nominal restoration is 1500 energy.

type zero. Clear the power-bomb effect flag, end the special palette, restore normal movement and

so the next update travels away from the wall.

the current beam angle into one of five facing-aware Samus frames, so rotating the scan changes aim
without advancing an ordinary pose animation.
